meta.name: Microsoft Fabric Data Engineer Associate (DP-700)
meta.notes: Initial pack — 10 scenario-style questions across the three DP-700 domains: implement and manage an analytics solution, ingest and transform data, monitor and optimize. | 2026-05-23 keyword-balance pass

questions.question: A team has a curated Delta table in ADLS Gen2 that other Microsoft Fabric workspaces should query without copying or scheduling. The data engineer needs to expose the table inside a lakehouse so notebooks can read it as if it were local, while updates at the source remain immediately visible. Which feature meets the requirement?
options: Create a managed Delta table inside the lakehouse and load the data with a one-time ADLS Gen2 copy pipeline — copying the data breaks the single-copy principle of OneLake; a OneLake shortcut references the data in-place without duplicating it into a managed Delta table
Mount the storage account inside the workspace using a notebook with a shared access signature on every session
Schedule a Data Pipeline copy activity each hour to refresh a lakehouse Delta copy of the source folder location
Configure a OneLake shortcut in the lakehouse Tables area that targets the external ADLS Gen2 location holding the data
questions.explanation: OneLake shortcuts create a virtual reference to data stored outside the lakehouse (ADLS Gen2, Amazon S3, Dataverse, or another OneLake item) with no data copy. The lakehouse exposes the data as a normal Delta table; notebooks and SQL endpoint queries read the live source. Loading or scheduled copies duplicate storage and add latency, and SAS mounts are not the supported pattern in Fabric.

questions.question: An analytics team must run T-SQL DDL and DML such as MERGE, CREATE PROCEDURE, and multi-statement transactions against curated tables in Fabric. They also want every change to be ACID-compliant via Delta under the hood. Which Fabric item natively supports T-SQL writes (insert, update, delete) on top of Delta?
options: Lakehouse, whose SQL analytics endpoint allows full T-SQL SELECT plus INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE — false; the SQL analytics endpoint on a lakehouse supports read-only T-SQL SELECT queries over Delta tables, not DML operations; only a Warehouse persists data in delta format with full DDL and DML
Warehouse, which provides a full T-SQL DDL and DML surface and persists each table as Delta in OneLake
KQL Database, which offers Kusto-style ingestion plus full T-SQL DDL on the materialized result tables
Eventhouse, where T-SQL is the primary write language for all streaming aggregations and reference tables
questions.explanation: The Fabric Warehouse exposes a full T-SQL surface — DDL, DML, multi-statement transactions, and stored procedures — and persists each table as Delta Parquet in OneLake. The Lakehouse SQL analytics endpoint is read-only T-SQL; writes go through Spark or Dataflows. KQL Database and Eventhouse target KQL workloads, not T-SQL writes.

questions.question: A Dataflow Gen2 ingests several large CSV files, applies multiple Power Query merges, and writes the result to a lakehouse table. Refreshes are unexpectedly slow and the engineer notices repeated re-evaluation of the same merge inputs across query steps. Which Dataflow Gen2 capability is designed to fix this?
options: Disable staging on every query so each step runs end-to-end in memory without writing intermediate results to the lakehouse — disabling staging forces all query execution into the dataflow engine memory, which causes out-of-memory failures on large lakehouse datasets
Enable staging on the merged queries so intermediate results land in the Fabric staging lakehouse and are reused
Switch the dataflow output destination to a warehouse and rely on T-SQL to push down the joins after the load
Convert each query into a separate dataflow and chain them with manual refresh-on-success orchestration triggers
questions.explanation: Dataflows Gen2 stages query results in a hidden Fabric lakehouse and warehouse when staging is enabled. Downstream queries (merges, joins) then read the staged intermediate instead of re-evaluating sources, which dramatically reduces redundant work. Disabling staging makes the problem worse, and switching destinations or chaining dataflows does not address repeated merge evaluation.

questions.question: A Fabric workspace pipeline must read from an Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 account that is firewalled to a virtual network. The team prefers not to manage stored credentials or service principal secrets in connection strings. Which Fabric feature lets the workspace authenticate to the storage account using its own Microsoft Entra identity?
options: A workspace identity, which is a Microsoft Entra service principal owned by the workspace and used by supported items

A user-assigned managed identity attached to the capacity and shared across all workspaces — a shared managed identity is not bound to a single workspace's entra principal and does not own the Microsoft Fabric workspace resources as the workspace identity does
An on-premises data gateway running in the customer datacenter with a stored access key for the storage account
A personal access token tied to the workspace creator, refreshed automatically by the Fabric runtime each day
questions.explanation: A Fabric workspace identity is a managed Microsoft Entra service principal scoped to that workspace. Supported items (Pipelines, Dataflows Gen2, Eventstream) can use it to access trusted resources such as ADLS Gen2 behind a firewall — no stored secrets needed. Capacity-level or tenant-wide identities and personal access tokens are not the supported pattern, and on-prem gateways are for on-prem sources, not cloud-firewalled storage.

questions.question: A team must ingest a high-volume IoT telemetry stream from Azure Event Hubs into Fabric, apply windowed aggregations, and land both raw events and aggregates in a KQL database for sub-second querying. They want a low-code visual canvas to design the pipeline. Which Fabric item should they use?
options: A Data Pipeline with a Copy Activity scheduled every minute to pull batches from Event Hubs into the KQL database
A Dataflow Gen2 in incremental refresh mode that connects to Event Hubs and writes to a managed lakehouse table
An Eventstream that ingests from Event Hubs, applies streaming transformations, and writes to the KQL database
A Spark Structured Streaming notebook reading Event Hubs and writing micro-batches into a Delta lakehouse table
questions.explanation: Eventstream is Fabric's no-code/low-code real-time ingestion item. It connects to streaming sources (Event Hubs, IoT Hub, Kafka, Custom App), supports inline transformations and windowed aggregations on a visual canvas, and writes to destinations such as a KQL database, lakehouse, or another Eventstream. Pipelines are batch, Dataflows Gen2 are not stream-native, and Spark notebooks work but are not the low-code canvas the requirement specifies.

questions.question: A Power BI report in Direct Lake mode on a 200-million-row Delta table in a Fabric lakehouse is slower than expected. The engineer reads that a Fabric-specific Parquet write optimization can reorder rows and dictionary-encode them for faster scans by the Power BI engine. Which optimization should be enabled?
options: Z-Order clustering on every column of the table so each scan for Direct Lake reads the smallest possible set of row groups — Z-Order is a Databricks Delta Lake feature; it does not exist in Microsoft Fabric and is not an optimization applicable to Direct Lake mode
V-Order, a write-time Parquet optimization that improves scan speed for Direct Lake and SQL endpoint queries
Liquid clustering, which dynamically reorganizes the table without the engineer specifying any cluster keys
ZSTD compression at level 22, which trades extra CPU on write for a much smaller on-disk Parquet file size
questions.explanation: V-Order is Fabric's write-time Parquet optimization. It applies a special sort, row-group sizing, and dictionary encoding so the Power BI Direct Lake engine and the Fabric SQL endpoint scan the files faster — often 10–50 percent faster. Z-Order helps file pruning by clustering but is a Databricks/Delta feature less tuned to Power BI; liquid clustering and ultra-high ZSTD do not provide the same Power BI scan boost.

questions.question: A development workspace contains lakehouses, notebooks, and reports that must be promoted to Test and then Production workspaces with item references rewritten and a manual approval gate before Production. Which Fabric feature provides this multi-stage promotion natively?
options: Git integration with a feature branch per workspace, where each pull request merged to main triggers a manual deployment — Git integration provides version control but does not define promotion stages with manual approval gates between Development, Test, and Production environments

A workspace clone created from the Fabric Admin portal whenever a release candidate is ready for promotion to Test — workspace clones copy the current state once but do not define repeatable promotion stages with approval gates between environments
A Data Pipeline that copies each item's JSON definition from one workspace to another on a recurring schedule
A Fabric deployment pipeline with Development, Test, and Production stages and a manual deploy step between them
questions.explanation: Fabric deployment pipelines model a multi-stage release flow — typically Development → Test → Production — for supported items including lakehouses, notebooks, semantic models, and reports. They handle item references between stages and require a manual deploy step that supports approvals. Git integration handles source control but does not orchestrate stage promotion; Data Pipelines and workspace clones are not stage-aware deployment tools.

questions.question: After a Spark job runs daily, a Fabric capacity reports sustained smoothing-related throttling for several hours and dashboard refreshes start to queue. The admin needs to identify which items consumed the most capacity units (CUs) to plan a redesign. Which built-in tool exposes per-item CU consumption over time?
options: The Fabric Capacity Metrics app installed from AppSource and pointed at the capacity to view per-item CU usage
The Monitoring hub in the workspace, which lists per-item run status but does not break down CU consumption by item
Azure Monitor diagnostic settings on the Fabric tenant, which export CU usage events to a Log Analytics workspace
The Power BI Premium Capacity admin view, which reports Premium Gen2 CU usage for legacy workspaces only
questions.explanation: The Microsoft Fabric Capacity Metrics app is the supported tool for analyzing capacity unit (CU) consumption. It exposes per-item CU usage, smoothing and burst behavior, throttling, and overage time-series so admins can identify heavy items and right-size the capacity. The Monitoring hub shows job run status, not capacity economics, and Azure Monitor and the legacy Premium view do not provide Fabric per-item CU detail.

questions.question: A team needs to make an Azure SQL Database queryable inside Fabric with near-real-time replication, but without writing change data capture or running ETL jobs. The replicated copy should appear as a read-only Delta source in OneLake. Which Fabric capability fits?
options: A Dataflow Gen2 with incremental refresh that polls the source database every minute and reads changed rows into a OneLake Delta table — Dataflow Gen2 incremental refresh checks for changes on a schedule, not continuously; it introduces latency and complexity compared to native Mirroring replication into OneLake
A Data Pipeline ForEach activity that runs a Copy activity per table on a five-minute schedule, full refresh
Mirroring, which continuously replicates the source database into OneLake as read-only Delta tables with low latency

A linked server in the Fabric warehouse that issues federated queries to read from the source database on demand — federated queries introduce latency on every read and depend on the source database remaining available at query time
questions.explanation: Fabric Mirroring (for Azure SQL DB, Cosmos DB, Snowflake, and other supported sources) continuously replicates source data into OneLake as read-only Delta tables with near-real-time latency. No ETL or CDC code is needed; consumers query the replicated Delta tables through the lakehouse SQL endpoint or Power BI. Dataflows and scheduled pipelines add polling latency, and Fabric has no SQL Server-style linked-server feature.

questions.question: A semantic model on a 1.5-billion-row Delta table in a lakehouse must serve interactive Power BI reports with no scheduled import refresh and without falling back to DirectQuery's per-visual query cost. The team wants the engine to read Parquet directly from OneLake into memory on demand. Which semantic model storage mode meets the requirement?
options: Import mode, where the model loads a full copy of the data into VertiPaq memory from OneLake — Import mode reads the data from OneLake on refresh and stores a compressed in-memory copy; it does not load Parquet column segments directly from OneLake on demand as Direct Lake mode does
DirectQuery mode, where each visual issues a live SQL query through the lakehouse SQL analytics endpoint
Direct Lake mode, where the model loads Parquet column segments directly from OneLake into memory on demand
Dual mode, where each table is replicated into both Import and DirectQuery and the engine picks at query time
questions.explanation: Direct Lake is a Fabric-only semantic-model storage mode that reads Delta/Parquet column segments directly from OneLake into the Power BI engine without an import refresh and without issuing per-visual DirectQuery requests. It delivers Import-like query performance with no refresh schedule on top of lakehouse or warehouse Delta tables — typically paired with V-Order for best results.
